Let

\[
P(x,y):\quad f(xy)\le yf(x)+f(y)\qquad \text{for all }x,y\in\mathbb R.
\]

We will prove that \(f\) must be identically zero.

---

### 1. Determine \(f(-1)\)

Let

\[
c=f(-1).
\]

For any \(t\in\mathbb R\), apply \(P(-1,t)\):

\[
f(-t)\le t f(-1)+f(t)=tc+f(t),
\]

so

\[
f(-t)-f(t)\le tc. \tag{1}
\]

Now apply \(P(-1,-t)\):

\[
f(t)\le -t f(-1)+f(-t)=-tc+f(-t),
\]

so

\[
f(-t)-f(t)\ge tc. \tag{2}
\]

From (1) and (2),

\[
f(-t)-f(t)=tc \qquad \text{for all }t\in\mathbb R. \tag{3}
\]

Next apply \(P(t,-1)\):

\[
f(-t)\le -f(t)+f(-1)=-f(t)+c,
\]

so

\[
f(-t)-f(t)\le c. \tag{4}
\]

Using (3) in (4), we get

\[
tc\le c \qquad \text{for all }t\in\mathbb R.
\]

Take \(t=0\):

\[
0\le c \implies c\ge 0.
\]

Take \(t=2\):

\[
2c\le c \implies c\le 0.
\]

Hence

\[
c=f(-1)=0.
\]

---

### 2. \(f\) is even and nonpositive

From (3) with \(c=0\),

\[
f(-t)-f(t)=0,
\]

so

\[
f(-t)=f(t)\qquad \text{for all }t\in\mathbb R.
\]

Thus \(f\) is even.

Now use \(P(t,-1)\) again. Since \(f(-1)=0\),

\[
f(-t)\le -f(t).
\]

Because \(f\) is even, \(f(-t)=f(t)\), so

\[
f(t)\le -f(t),
\]

which gives

\[
2f(t)\le 0.
\]

Therefore

\[
f(t)\le 0 \qquad \text{for all }t\in\mathbb R. \tag{5}
\]

---

### 3. Determine \(f(0)\)

From (5), we know \(f(0)\le 0\). Suppose \(f(0)<0\). Apply \(P(0,2)\):

\[
f(0)\le 2f(0)+f(2),
\]

so

\[
f(2)\ge -f(0)>0.
\]

But this contradicts \(f(2)\le 0\) from (5). Therefore \(f(0)\not<0\), so

\[
f(0)\ge 0.
\]

Combined with \(f(0)\le 0\), we obtain

\[
f(0)=0.
\]

---

### 4. Finish the proof

For any \(y\in\mathbb R\), apply \(P(0,y)\):

\[
f(0)\le yf(0)+f(y).
\]

Since \(f(0)=0\), this becomes

\[
0\le f(y).
\]

Together with \(f(y)\le 0\) from (5), we get

\[
f(y)=0
\]

for every \(y\in\mathbb R\).

Finally, the zero function clearly satisfies

\[
0\le 0+0
\]

for all \(x,y\in\mathbb R\).

Hence the only solution is

\[
\boxed{f(x)=0\text{ for all }x\in\mathbb R}
\]
